title: Dennis Randall: Content
body_text: Dennis Randall: Content Home | Creativity | Community | Content | Connection | Cool Tools | Site Map | Resume The Best of Randall's Backyard Science While at FEN I created more than 1,500 original editorial items including the ones featured below. I think they're some of the best articles I've written and produced for FamilyEducation. Enjoy! Weather | Astronomy | The Environment | Just for Fun | Top Weather: Weather : Check out these cool links to some weather hot spots. Backyard Weather Station : Ever think of building a backyard weather station with your kids? It's fun, easy, and makes a great family project! Here's how... How Rain Works -- Science for Kids : Is your kid wondering what this drought is all about? While you weather this dry spell, turn your kid into a weatherperson and your home into a weather station! Also, some tips on saving water ... The Science of Snow : Snowflakes and kids are made for each other. You can use your children's natural curiosity about snow as a gateway into scientific exploration. Here's a primer. Let it Snow! Here's a cool quiz with nifty questions like: What is the biggest snowflake on record? Bet you can't guess... For more great weather information for kids visit... Snow Crystals : While no two snowflakes are alike, they can be generally classified into six basic patterns as a result of unique atmospheric conditions present at the crystal's birth. Think of them as a kind of "cloud diary" and a record of conditions aloft. Snow Sculptures : When it comes to playing in the snow, kids love it and we adults often get cold feet. Literally. This doesn't have to be the case. Weather | Astronomy | The Environment | Just for Fun | Top Astronomy: The Night Sky : Some of the best backyard science can be found over your head! body_text: Dennis Randall: Cool Tools Home | Creativity | Community | Content | Connection | Cool Tools | Site Map | Resume More than anything, a Web site needs to be useful and informative. Next, it needs to be fun to use. Fun on the Web means interactive. In the world of the Web, community sits at the top of the interactive food-chain. We've added a few applications you can use to help make your site interactive and fun. The beauty is they're all FREE. A good price for anyone on a budget ;-) Image Editors: All the graphics on this Web site were created or edited using PaintShop Pro: v4.12. While there are newer versions of Paint Shop pro, they all contain a "drop dead after 30 day" feature. The 4.12 release was the last with an infinite evaluation period . Honor suggests that you really should discontinue use after 30 days if you don't purchase it. There's a nag screen advising me that I'm on the 413th day of my 30 day evaluation trial. PaintShop pro was created by the good folks at Jasc Software, Inc. and it's, IMHO, one of the very best image editors available today. Top Organization: Ten Quick Tips for Better Site Design Tom Karlo put this list together to help provide pointers and direction for folks who know HTML and want to produce better site designs. His list is more concerned with the issues of designing pages than the technical problems of HTML or Photoshop and is a must read for any wannabe webmaster. The Tips : 1. Keep your goal in sight 2. Design sites, not pages 3. Never design in HTML 4. Write down your design 5. Go for consistency 6. Templates 7. Think like a user 8. Ask your users what they see 9. Content is king 10. Don't link for the heck of it 1 . Keep your goal in mind Too often, people forget why the site they're designing is being put up. The purpose of designing a site carefully is not to make it look cool, or win awards. It's to accomplish the intended goal of the site. If you're making a site for a company, sometimes the goal is simply to distribute information about the firm. Often, however, the real goal is to sell or advertise some product of the company. Obviously, the structure and design of the site would have to vary greatly depending on which of these two objectives was viewed as the primary one. Note, however, that you usually will have more than one goal in building a site. Before starting a project, carefully write down a statement of the goals of the site. How do you know what your goals are? Simple. Ask your client. If you're your own client

title: The Athens Digest - What color is the rainbow?
body_text: The Athens Digest - What color is the rainbow? Home | Creativity | Community | Content | Connection | Cool Tools | Site Map | Resume My Grandfather's House by Dennis Randall We all carry the memories of perfect childhood summers when we stood still and time rolled out from under us. Effortless, endless lazy days of joy and tranquillity. I found my perfect summer in Plympton, Massachusetts at my grandfather's house. "...his words transformed the kitchen into the whaling grounds and ships..." His home was a three hundred year old farmhouse located deep in the forest. The house had no electricity, running water or central heating. With the exception of age it was virtually unchanged from that day in the 1650's when it was built. It was a little island in time that had somehow escaped the benefits of the 20th century. My grandfather lived alone in the house and each summer I would stay with him for a few weeks. Simple but delicious meals were prepared on an ancient wood cookstove located in a corner of the kitchen. The stove was a smokey thing and everything we ate or wore had the comfortable mellow-brown flavor of wood. Food and milk was kept cool and safe in a wobbly wooden bucket at the bottom of a deep stone well. Even in the hottest days of August, water from that well was cold and clear. In the evenings, after dinner and dishes were finished, he and I would sit for hours at the kitchen table and I listened as he told story after story. Shadows from the flickering yellow light of the kerosene lamp moved on the walls as he unraveled countless tales of knights and unicorns, leprechauns, elves and the travels of Gulliver. "Look over there," he would say pointing to the shelf above the stove, "those three boxes of cereal are just like the sails on a whaling ship. And, over there, that butter dish looks just like the dories the men would use to hunt the Great White Whale." His words transformed the kitchen into the whaling grounds and ships from the story of Moby Dick. Shadows became the characters and crew and the coat rack with my grandfathers felt hat came alive as the stern and possessed Captain Ahab. A long story like Moby Dick would take several nights to tell. The evening hours my grandfather and I would spend around the kerosene lamp became the center of my summer days. "Hold it from the inside and look out through its eyes. Hear its story." I have so many recollections of that kitchen as the deck of a sailing ship or the treasure mines of King Solomon that it is difficult to recall how the place really appeared. The remembrances and images of his stories are more vivid than my memories of that room in daylight. My grandfather would ask, in fact demand, that I see things in a different way. "Look at something and then look at the things around it, ask questions of it," he would say, "What else does it look like? How does it feel and how did it get there? body_text: The Athens Digest - What color is the rainbow? Home | Creativity | Community | Content | Connection | Cool Tools | Site Map | Resume Part Two by Dennis N. Randall Lighting After a hard day at work, in the fields or factory, most people returned home, ate whatever dinner was ready, and collapsed until the start of the next work day. Folks who wished to stay up and socialize or finish chores often did so in dim, candle lit rooms. By the standards of yesterday, our homes blaze with the brilliance of day. A twenty-five watt bulb burns with the light of more than 200 candles. An average family room today has about 175 watts of light - or the equivalent of more than 1,400 candles. Horses Horses were common forms of transportation and their pollutants were everywhere. The early street sweepers and sanitation men who were hired to keep the streets clean were not just picking up gum wrappers. In twelve months a city with 15,000 horses produces enough manure to cover an acre of ground to the depth of 175 feet. That amount of waste, when mixed with summer rains and the hot August sun turned large cities like Boston, New York, and Chicago into the worst kind of steam baths imaginable. Rural towns and villages werent much better. The areas around hitching posts were open cesspools. When the rains came, everything mixed with mud. The quaint wooden boardwalks were not constructed as a convenience. They were a necessity. Civil Rights Racial and religious minorities were at the mercy of the times. In 1836 a school for black children was burned to the ground by an angry white mob in Canton, Connecticut. Slavery was the law of the land until it was ended by the civil war and a constitutional amendment. Between 1882 and 1903, more than 3,300 people were lynched across the United States. Lynching of blacks alone totaled 2,060. Guilt or innocence made little difference to a mob driven by a blood lust. Lynching went far beyond simple hanging and often include anything from boiling the victim alive, castration, and torture to burning at the stake. Discrimination in the workplace was rampant. Blacks, Jews, and Catholics were not allowed to work at many jobs. The law of the land did not protect minorities in the good old days. Pollution As cities became industrialized, the air was modernized. Smoke stacks were considered a sign of progress and large industrialized cities had hundreds, if not thousands, of them. Clouds of pollutants - sulfur, ammonia, and coal dust  settled on laundry, lungs, and gardens. Tanneries with their slaughter houses, bone boiling, and manure added their own unique flavor to the air around them. Government regulations to protect citizens and the environment were nonexistent. Business resisted then, as much as it does today, any attempt to make it clean up its act. Pollution was accepted as the necessary price of progress. Food Food in the good old days wasnt always that good. Reports abound of stores selling food products that were adulterated

title: The Athens Digest - What color is the rainbow?
body_text: The Athens Digest - What color is the rainbow? Home | Creativity | Community | Content | Connection | Cool Tools | Site Map | Resume by Dennis N. Randall Life in the 1800s has taken on an almost Utopian quality in the minds of many Americans. The images associated with this era of our history are, on the surface, pleasant to recall: one room school houses with a heavy dose of the 3 Rs; rugged self-reliance; living close to the earth, no income tax, steam-powered railroads and individual freedom. Topics: A Typical Workday Child Labor Workplace Safety Industry and Energy The Standard of Living Hard Times All-in-all, we seem to recall a well-scrubbed past taken from the pages of those Currier & Ives prints. Maybe, as we cross into the next century, it's time to take another look at the so-called "good old days." On the job Workdays in the mid to late 1800s were long and hard. The average worker could expect to labor anywhere from ten to fourteen hours a day, six days a week. A sixty or eighty hour work week was the rule, not the exception. By 1830, a skilled worker or experienced machinist earned as much as $1.25 a day. However, jobs that paid that well were uncommon. An average worker could expect to earn between fifty and seventy-five cents a day. A woman lucky enough to find a paying job earned far less than a man. Her standard wage was anywhere from half to two-thirds less than her male counterpart. Unions were almost unheard of. Where they existed they were considered, by factory owners and industrialists, to be "un-American." When horse-car drivers in New York City demanded that their traditional 16-hour work day be reduced to only 12 hours, their demands were branded as "communistic" by state assemblyman Teddy Roosevelt. When strikes did occur, they were often put down by troops and militiamen. Child labor Children often worked the same long hours as their parents. By 1900 there were nearly two million children under fifteen years of age working in factories across the nation. Child labor was in great demand by employers who considered children to be a bargain. Kids were paid between $1.50 and $2.50 a week for up to 84 hours of work. (Two or three cents an hour was considered low pay, even by the standards of the day.) Safety in the workplace In the days before government regulations and the union movement, the place where you worked could easily become the place where you died. President Harrison observed in 1892 that, "American workmen are subjected to peril of life and limb as great as a soldier in time of war." During the 1890s it was estimated that nearly a million workers were killed or injured each year in the work place. Power shafts and belts to drive the machines were open and unprotected. Factories were dimly lighted and the workers' machines and equipment were not equipped with the safety devices now required by law. The rule of thumb, for those lucky enough to still have one, was, "if you take the job - you assume the risk." Rail

body_text: Washington- new HTML Template by Dennis Randall Travel Tips Hiking & Walking National Parks Museums Our nation's capital can be an overwhelming adventure -- you could spend a lifetime in the city and still not see everything! The key is: Plan your time wisely. The links below will help you get started. Editor's Pick -- Tourmobile : Don't walk, don't drive -- take a guided tour -- there are more than 20 to choose from. The Tourmobile is a privately operated, licensed concession of the National Park Service. Editor's Pick -- Capital Children's Museum -- Interactive, hands-on museum where children and adults find learning fun and rewarding. 800 3rd St., NE, Washington, DC 20002 (near Union Station Metro station ). (202) 543-8600. Daily, 10:00 a.m. -- 5:00 p.m. Admission: $6 adults and children; children under 2, free. _________________________________________ Travel Tips: Washington is not a car-friendly city. Parking is expensive and next to impossible to find. When it comes to getting around, your best bet is a good map and a guided tour (there are tons of them) or the city's excellent Metro system. Visiting almost any place in the city requires walking, and lots of it! If you've got little ones with you we recommend a well-stocked stroller -- by the end of the day, the kids will need it. Summer in DC can be very hot and humid with an average temperature of 82 degrees. So, bring lots of water along -- unless you like to spend $2.00 and up for a can of cold soda. _________________________________________ Hiking/Walking The city is crisscrossed with 16 trails providing more than 50 miles of hiking experience in northwest Washington. All trails are within easy walking distance of local Metro stations. Since you'll likely be traveling with kids, we've listed only trails less than 2 miles long. For a complete list, chect the D.C. Trail Guide. Editor's Pick -- Dumbarton Oaks Trail (trail goes through the beautiful 27-acre Dumbarton Oaks Park and is an ideal walk for young kids -- only 0.8 mile) Editor's Pick -- D.C. Trail Guide (Links to all Washington hiking and walking trails) Former trolley right of way (0.6 mile) Wesley Heights Trail (0.8 mile) Normanstone Trail (0.9 mile) Soapstone Valley Trail (0.9 mile) Whitehaven Trail (1 mile) Melvin Hazen Trail (1.1 mile) Battery Kemble Trail (1.3 miles) _________________________________________ National Parks There are 51 national parks and historic sites in and around Washington. Most involve quite a bit of walking and the larger sites should be considered all-day events. Visitors to Washington have two options: visit dozens of places and leave with only vague impressions; or, visit only a few places and explore each one in-depth. We favor a blend both styles -- select a few for in-depth exploration and several others for quick visits. title: Money for Old Rope - Adbars
body_text: Money for Old Rope - Adbars A word about adbars For many people, the idea of being paid to use the Internet is strange. "Why would anyone want to give me their money ?", I hear you asking. The answer is that you are a potential purchaser of goods and services, and suppliers want to advertise to you. "But I hate adverts!" Adbars simply sit there on your screen and other than taking up a little screen space, they won't bother you at all. No one is asking you to study the adverts on your pc screen , you may have to run the mouse over them every few minutes, but you needn't actually buy anything. The higher the resolution of your screen, the less space they occupy. "What is an Adbar ?" An adbar is a banner. The size varies, but the ones I use are about half an inch high, and the full width of my screen. The adbars may sit at the top or bottom of your screen. You can turn them off, and they go away, but then so does your income :-( "How much can I earn?" The going rate differs, but most pay about 30p per hour. Not alot. You can, however have a few going at the same time and your income then starts to look attractive. I usually have two or three going, and hardly notice the reduction in screen size at all. I put them both at the top, move the taskbar over to the right hand side, and (gasp - I confess) sometimes I adjust the picture height of my monitor to eliminate them completely! Think about the last month. How many hours did you spend on the Internet ? Half an hour each evening maybe ? Well with two adbars up and running, thats over £9 you could have had. If you're still paying for your Internet phone calls - £9 will more than likely have covered your phone call costs, or if you're on a free internet service (and we all should be by now), it is £9 for you to save or spend as you like. Payment is usually made by cheque, when your dues exceed a certain amount. So, you won't get a cheque every month from each one, but you don't lose out either because earnings are carried forward at the end of the month until there is enough in the pot to trigger the payment. There's one more thing. In addition to signing up, these companies encourage you to recruit others. Now, I'd be lying if I said all this about adbars was purely for your education. I have a vested interest in persuading you to join! My pennies also increase if you sign up using the links I give. Consider, you have your own circle of friends, and if in turn you ask them to join up too, you will increase your earnings in the same way. Remember, it is not going to cost your friends anything to join - when you refer a friend to the service, you are not asking them to spend - you are giving them an opportunity to earn. Heads you win, Tails you win ! Return......

title: The Picture Gallery
body_text: The Picture Gallery 3rd January 1999 Chris G4FZN "I'm the author of these pages. Thanks for stopping by - I hope you find most of these pages interesting and informative. I'm licenced to operate on all of the amateur radio bands, but my main interest is VHF and UHF. I'm in the Richmond Raynet Group, who occasionally provide emergency communications for user services in this area. When I'm not playing radio, I play keyboard for a local band called "The Pulse". There are five of us, a superb lead guitarist, a bass guitarist, drummer (or is it called "percussionist" these days ?), a male vocalist, and yours truly on keys. Our music can be best described as "rock classics", - you know them all - numbers from the Rolling Stones, Zombies, Troggs, Beatles which we blend together with numbers from Bruce Springsteen and the Eagles to give the subtle change of tempo. Add to that lot the Wilson Pickett song, "Midnight Hour" and the Tommy James number, "Mony Mony" and others like that, and you'll see we've got a fantastic mix of music to play. Some of our best performances have been to biker's meets and music festivals - I don't think we'd go down very well at a house/garage party or a bass 'n drum rave!!!! EMail: chris_kirby@geocities.com Pauline G8HQW "Hi, I'm Pauline. I'm an audiologist at a local hospital. Have you had your hearing tested recently? Its amazing how many people haven't. I try to keep fit by working out three times a week in the gym at the Fitness Centre. " EMail: pjkirby@yahoo.com Stephen 2E1DZK "Hello from Stephen. I'm a 6th form student at Richmond School. There is an Amateur Radio Club which meets almost every lunchtime. You will often our club callsign GX0RYS active on 20m and other bands. The club also operates on the 70cms amateur band, and operates a packet radio station. You can send a message to us at: GX0RYS@GB7CYM.#19.GBR.EU. Mr Vann, (G3RLV) is the Science teacher who runs the school Radio Club, and without him we wouldn't be able to meet. I support Luton Town Football Club because I was born at the Luton & Dunstable hospital in 1982." EMail: sjkirby@yahoo.com Simon 2E1GUN "Hello, Simon here. My favourite sports are football and hockey. I play hockey for Richmond School and have played for the County. The soccer team I support is Arsenal Football Club , (that's their strip I'm wearing) and I check out their Web pages from time to time. Don't you think my callsign is brill for an Aresnal supporter - their nickname is the GUNNERS !! EMail: scwkirby@yahoo.com Arthur G6FGE "Hello, I'm Arthur, a retired civil engineer who has been licenced ten years, but I'm not very active on the bands. Colin G6AHF "Where's my picture gone?" Judith G4XMG © 1999 Chris Kirby Return to Chris Kirby's Home Page Return to Geocities

title: Free Shares from Totalise ISP
body_text: Free Shares from Totalise ISP Free Shares Totalise is an Internet Service Provider with a difference. They are currently listed on the Ofex market, but they have announced they expect to be listed on AIM (Alternative Investment Market) within three months (from 1st June). With Totalise you receive shares for (a) Joining up, (b) Using them as your ISP, (c) sending emails using them, and (d) recommending new users. I have been with Totalise for several months, and have amassed a reasonable number of shares. The share price varies, at the time of writing it is around 45p, but has been over £1 and as low as 25p. You can sell Totalise shares through a broker. The other good thing about Totalise is that their Tech Support is FREE - so if you want expert technical help free of charge, Totalise is a good ISP to choose. Totalise charges local rate for access to the Internet. It is an 0845 number. How many shares can I earn with Totalise ? Should you decide to sign up with Totalise , please be kind enough to enter my user name " maybe " into the referral box. Return......

title: Scotch Corner Gateway
body_text: Scotch Corner Gateway The "Scotch Corner" Gateway Key: 1 Time switch 2 Mobile phone in hands-free kit for monitoring audio 3 Yaesu FT2600 2m tcvr 4 Home brew interface 5 Switch mode PSU 6 ISDN terminal adaptor 7 PC - 233 MHz Pentium 8 BT Easyreach pager for emergency shutdown 9 VHF / UHF diplexor 10 70cm TX / Rx (Yes; we do have wallpaper at this QTH - but the gateway is in the loft to keep the xyl happy! ) NoV Holders: G4FZN & G8HQW & 2E1GUN Transmit: 14dBw erp Maximum Deviation: +/- 2.5kHz Antenna: Omnidirectional (vertical polarization) Frequencies: 145.3375MHz & 431.200MHz Identification: Morse Code, 22wpm Audio frequency 459Hz Coverage map of the Scotch Corner Gateway (100kB) The Scotch Corner Gateway operates on 145.3375MHz. eQSO software is usually operated. No repeater shift is required, and no access tones are needed. The gateway operates a simple squelch system, which means any signal on the frequency will be accepted. In the future, if more internet gateways become operational, and QRM becomes more of a problem, the Scotch Corner Gateway may have to resort to CTCSS tone squelch. Chris, G4FZN will resist this for as long as possible! Incoming signals are re-radiated on 431.200MHz when the gateway is in operation. (see below) Being a simplex system, the gateway cannot relay signals from one radio user in the North East to another radio user in the North East. Most stations in this area are able to hear the other users direct, but there are times when the gateway can hear two stations who can't hear each other. In this situation, a repeater could assist communications BUT a simplex gateway can not help matters. Why is this? Because, unlike a duplex repeater with a frequency split, a simplex gateway cannot transmit and receive at the same time. For this reason, the 70cms frequency (431.200MHz) has been added recently. The output power on 431.200MHz is very low - 3 watts erp - however the audio from the internet is mixed with audio from the two metre receiver and retransmitted on 431.200. At the time of writing, no 70cm receive frequency is available. Hours of Operation During weekdays, the Scotch Corner gateway is active from 7am to 10am, and from 4pm through to midnight. At weekends, operation if from 7am through to 1am without a gap. The RSGB news, read by Jeremy Boot, G4NJH, is transmitted at 10.30am on Sunday mornings. Alternatively, you can click here to listen now in Real Audio. Who is welcome to use it? All licenced amateurs are very welcome to use the gateway. title: GB3HG 2m repeater
body_text: GB3HG 2m repeater The unofficial GB3HG web site by Chris Kirby, G4FZN Updated September 2000 GB3HG is still located on Bilsdale West Moor, North Yorkshire, IO94ki Frequencies CTCSS Timeout 145.025MHz (Input) / 145.625MHz (output) No CTCSS activation Timeout period - 3 minutes This page used to be hosted at http://www.qsl.net/gb3hg but for some reason it has been made "forbidden" !!! New Repeater Site Coverage Map GB3HG is moving QTH to Richmond. A coverage prediction map generated by NTL's Aspect system is now available showing the predicted coverage from the new site at Richmond. There are two versions available, the first is a low resolution map, and the second is a fine detail map suitable for printing. Click here to view the low resolution map. (189kB) (High compression/Poor quality) Click here to view the high resolution map. (925kB) (Recommended for printing) click the right mouse button over the image to save it to disc GB3HG is still poorly ! The repeater (at it's current site) has been suffering from an intermittent interference problem which affects it's receive sensitivity. There is no suggestion that this interference is deliberate, but the exact cause has not yet been identified. Recently, the two folded dipole antennas were changed for open dipoles, and the coax termination at the top of the mast was double checked. Access to the mast costs the group £250 a time. Unfortunately, although the new antennas appear to be working well, the interference problem was not solved. When the interference is occurring, it consists of very sharp strong clicks on the received signal. If enough of these clicks happen, then the squelch closes, and the incoming signal is lost. There is a clear distinction to be heard between a weak signal - such as one might easily obtain by using a Slim Jim - , and a signal suffering due to the repeater's interference. The difference is in the sound of the background noise. The normally weak signal has a constant "hash" behind it, whereas an interfered signal has a characteristic "crackle". For the interference to manifest, the repeater must also be transmitting. It is not caused by blocking of the receiver (ie. desense) - as blocking causes gaussian noise, not the prickly noise which is heard. However, the effect is similar to that of desense insofar as a station can bring the repeater with a tone burst, but as soon as the repeater keys up, the incoming signal disappears, and the repeater shuts down immediately. ( A continuous transmission of 8 seconds is required to "latch" it on ). At a recent meeting of the repeater group (open only to invited members), a decision was taken to relocate the repeater to a site just north of Richmond, in North Yorkshire. The proposed site is used by Fresh AM radio for medium wave transmissions (1413kHz), but there are no other VHF services at the site. There is a mast which belongs to Castle Transmission nearby, but this is not the mast which it is proposed for HG to use. Two areas

title: GB3HG 2m repeater
body_text: GB3HG 2m repeater The unofficial GB3HG web site This is the site the repeater group tried to ban! Updated December 2001 GB3HG is still located on Bilsdale West Moor, North Yorkshire, IO94ki Frequencies CTCSS Timeout 145.025MHz (Input) 145.625MHz (Output) None Timeout period - 3 minutes This web site was originally hosted at www.qsl.net but due to a complaint by the secretary of the HG repeater group, Al Waller, who runs the qsl.net service has withdrawn the site. See for yourself --- http://www.qsl.net/gb3hg So much for "free speech" on the internet - eh ? Site relocation - soon! Site Clearance has now been obtained for the move to the new repeater site near Bedale, North Yorkshire. A meeting of the repeatwer group will be held in early January 2002, and if the go-ahead is given, you can expect the repater to be moved within days. The former alternative site at Richmond has been abandoned because the group found it difficult to maintain contact with the site owner. New Site Coverage Map I'm working on it! The Repeater Group The repeater is operated by the Harrogate Repeater Group . The group is affiliated to the RSGB , however membership of the repeater group is only available by invitation, and there is a maximum limit of forty members at any time. All membership applications received by the secretary to date have been turned down . Mine was one of them ;-( Voluntary donations are readily accepted from anyone and may be sent to the group treasurer, Brian Tindill, G4HVA, at "Hunters Moon", Station Road, Bedale, North Yorks, DL8 1SX. Brian's address is in the RSGB year book. How much should I send? I have been told by one member of the repeater group that the majority of donators give in excess of £20 per annum . The licence for GB3HG is a NOV (Notice of Variation) on the licence of the repeater keeper, Brian Dooks, G0RHI , the group secretary. Technical / Engineering work is carried out by Dave Smith, G4DAX . An impending and substantial site rental increase has forced the group to consider alternative sites. This was the subject of a special general meeting, held on 29 September 1999, in Boroughbridge. The purpose of the meeting was to select a new site for the repeater. title: GPS Page
body_text: GPS Page 31st January 1999 What is GPS ? The Global Positioning System (GPS) consists of 24 satellites in different orbits, each of which takes 12 hours to circle the earth. These satellites transmit information to earth, and can be received by members of the public - without any subscription needed - on a small GPS receiver. A GPS receiver requires visibility of at least three satellites, in order to compute its exact position on the earth's surface. For a three-dimensional fix, four satellites are required. Usually, there are between six and nine satellites "monitored" by the receiver. The writer owns a GPS II+. As happens, no sooner had I purchased this unti, that Garmin introduced a GPS III, which contains a complete road map of the UK. I have also seen a GPS III "pilot", which is an air based version of the GPS III, and it contains information useful to pilots, such as controlled air space charts, frequencies and air corridors. The GPS market is dominated by two companies, Garmin and Magellan. I have only experience of the Garmin products. If you have a Garmin GPS unit, it is well worth looking on the Garmin web site for updates to the software. My GPS II+ kept switching itself off for no apparent reason (Version 2.04 software), and I found an upgrade. The software is quite easy to upgrade, and full instructions are on the site. I am now running software version 2.07, and the unit no longer switches itself off! Waypoints To plot a course between two points (assuming they are less than a couple of hundred miles apart), you only need the start point, and the end point. Start up the engine, and away you go. However, in real-life, most courses are not as simple as that. At sea, you may wish to navigate around an island (!) or on land, you are forced into following public highways. So a course from A to B may well not be in a straight line. You need to set up a route. To do this, a number of points are chosen - called WAYPOINTS - which are then strung together in a fixed order, and - Hey presto - your route is again defined. Most GPS receivers can be programmed with waypoints. The GPS II+ can hold 500 of them, whereas other models can store 250 or less. Waypoints need not be points along a route, however, they are also used to mark reference points. I use waypoints to mark the location of amateur radio repeater stations, for example. As you move from one area to another, the GPS receiver can display the nearest "waypoints" (repeaters), and you always know which channel(s) to listen on for traffic reports. Waypoint files can be created, and uploaded into a GPS receiver using serial ASCII data and a suitable comms package. I use a program written by Garmin, called PCX5, however Procomm, or a similar communications program will do fine. The ASCII file below, which you are welcome to download, is a waypoint (.wpt) file of most of the amateur repeater stations in the UK. ukrptr.wpt Return to Chris Kirby's Home Page

body_text: _Anger_ Home Page Managing Anger Everyone experiences negative emotions such as anger, hurt, and feelings of betrayal, but most people have a difficult time expressing negative feelings--pariticularly anger--to others. Learning to manage this emotion can be rewarding. In some cases anger is a primary response to a negative situation; in others it may mask other feelings that you find even more difficult to tolerate, such as shame. In the latter case, learning to express anger constructively will help you uncover other important emotions as well. Freeing anger will allow you to feel more energized. You may have trouble showing anger in appropriate ways because our society does not encourage such expressions. Suppressing anger is ultimately destructive to your well-being--it can even make you physically sick. Due to the connection between mind and body, disease and anger go hand in hand. Truly happy people have far fewer diseases than unhappy people. Therefore, you need to think about the ways that your anger affects you physically. One way or another, you must learn to validate your anger and express it properly. Think of something that angers you. Write it down. Does this anger motivate you to change the situation in a constructive way? If you are suppressing your anger, think of an appropriate way to express it instead. What first step can you take? Use the following questions as guidelines to help you work through your thoughts. Why do you get angry? You may experience anger for a variety of reasons. Some examples include: Feeling Powerless. Do you feel angry when you cannot control your circumstances? Failure To Communicate. When someone does not communicate with you, or vice versa, that indifference will create anger. Think of a person in your life with whom you have trouble communicating. How does that obstacle anger you? Getting Defensive. People in powerful positions who must protect their image may become defensive and angry if challenged. Think about a situation that made you angry. Was your ego involved, or were you expressing your true beliefs and facing someone else's ego? In what way did either of you become defensive? Try to make an honest assessment of the situation. Feeling Betrayed. No one likes to be betrayed, especially by someone they trust. You feel hurt and angry by the experience and lose all faith in that person. It's important at such times to express your anger to the person. Don't hide your feelings--be honest. Feeling Hurt. Recall a time when someone hurt you. body_text: _Anger_ Home Page Managing Anger Everyone experiences negative emotions such as anger, hurt, and feelings of betrayal, but most people have a difficult time expressing negative feelings--pariticularly anger--to others. Learning to manage this emotion can be rewarding. In some cases anger is a primary response to a negative situation; in others it may mask other feelings that you find even more difficult to tolerate, such as shame. In the latter case, learning to express anger constructively will help you uncover other important emotions as well. Freeing anger will allow you to feel more energized. You may have trouble showing anger in appropriate ways because our society does not encourage such expressions. Suppressing anger is ultimately destructive to your well-being--it can even make you physically sick. Due to the connection between mind and body, disease and anger go hand in hand. Truly happy people have far fewer diseases than unhappy people. Therefore, you need to think about the ways that your anger affects you physically. One way or another, you must learn to validate your anger and express it properly. Think of something that angers you. Write it down. Does this anger motivate you to change the situation in a constructive way? If you are suppressing your anger, think of an appropriate way to express it instead. What first step can you take? Use the following questions as guidelines to help you work through your thoughts. Why do you get angry? You may experience anger for a variety of reasons. Some examples include: Feeling Powerless. Do you feel angry when you cannot control your circumstances? Failure To Communicate. When someone does not communicate with you, or vice versa, that indifference will create anger. Think of a person in your life with whom you have trouble communicating. How does that obstacle anger you? Getting Defensive. People in powerful positions who must protect their image may become defensive and angry if challenged. Think about a situation that made you angry. Was your ego involved, or were you expressing your true beliefs and facing someone else's ego? In what way did either of you become defensive? Try to make an honest assessment of the situation. Feeling Betrayed. No one likes to be betrayed, especially by someone they trust. You feel hurt and angry by the experience and lose all faith in that person. It's important at such times to express your anger to the person. Don't hide your feelings--be honest. Feeling Hurt. Recall a time when someone hurt you. title: AntiAging
body_text: AntiAging Skin sagging and wrinkling can be a sign of too much time spent on the beach or just a visible reminder of the relentless aging process. Cutaneous aging is a complex process affecting various layers of skin. Cutaneous aging includes the effects of gravity, expression lines, sleep lines, hormoral changes and genetic programming, and wind, smoke and chemical exposures. Innate or intrinsic aging, which affects skin by slow, irreversible degeneration of tissue. The consequences of innate aging can be observed over the entire surface of the body, including skin protected from the sun. As people age, innate or intrinsic aging changes their skin in ways that cause it to develop wrinkles. Few scientists had attributed skin aging to a single cause. But, recent research has revealed that a process long known to discolor and toughen food in storage also contributes to age-related changes in the skin. That process is primarily the chemical attachment of the sugar glucose to skin collagen without the aid of enzymes. When enzymes attach glucose to collagen, they do so for a specific purpose and at specific places. In contrast, the nonenzymatic process adds glucose haphazardly to any of several amino group sites along any available collagen molecule, as illustrated at the right (grey diamonds are glucose and black triangles are amino acids). The attachment of glucose to skin collagen triggers a series of spontaneous chemical reactions that culminate in the formation and eventual accumulation of irreversible cross-links between adjacent collagen molecules. The extensive cross-linking of collagen causes the loss of skin elasticity characteristic of aging. Therefore, "nonenzymatic glycosylation" of skin collagen is important, since it is the process that ages skin. The steps by which glucose alters skin collagen have been understood by food chemists for decades and only recently have biologists recognized that the same steps take place in the skin. The nonenzymatic glycosylation steps between glucose and collagen may seem complicated, but they are fairly straight forward compared with many biochemical reactions: A series of chemical reactions begin when an aldehyde group (CHO) of glucose and an amino group (NH 2 ) of a collagen molecule are attracted to each other. The glucose and amino group combine forming what is called a Schiff base. This combination is unstable and quickly rearranges itself into a stabler, but still reversible, substance known as an Amadori product. Long-lived collagen molecules persist in the body for years, allowing some of the Amadori products to slowly dehydrate and rearrange themselves yet again into new structures, called advanced glycosylation end-products (AGEs). title: kandy
body_text: kandy Hallo Biker! A g'miatliches Biken wa aongsogt! An alle, die ein Motorrad besitzen (in Unkenntnis der Grips'schen Ausrüstung mit diesem Werkzeug habe ich diese 'Mehl' an "alle" geschickt) und Lust haben, mit mir vom 3. bis 6.Juni 1999 (Do = Fronleichnam bis Sonntag) eine gemütliche Motorradtour zu unternehmen, sollen sich bitte bei mir zwecks Abklärung der weiteren Vorgangsweise melden. Route: GRAZ (0800) ==> Soboth (0900) ==> Tarvisio ==> Passo di Predil ==> Isonzotal ==> Nova Goriza ==> Triest (irgendwo zwischen T. und Pula übernachten) ==> Istrienrundfahrt ==> Brestova ==> Cres ==> Mali Losinij (2. Übernachtung) ==> Schwimmen, Faulenzen, Essen etc. (3. Übernachtung) ==> Abbazia ==> Postojna Paß ==> ??? ==> Graz. Änderungen vorbehalten (nur als Beispiel :schwimmen, faulenzen etc. könnte man ja jeden Tag machen) Da die Straßen über den Predilsattel, in Istrien und auf den Inseln nicht besonders gut sind, sind die Enduro-reiter (natürlich) im Vorteil; ist aber kein Ausschlußkriterium, da die Partie so und so unter dem Motto "Langsamer ist schneller" steht. Überlegt's es euch hms

title: Windmills of Barbados
body_text: Windmills of Barbados Windmills of Barbados Glossary Within Barbados, windmills are described using a number of local terms. Where appropriate, to keep this report consistent with other documents, I have used the local terms, as follows: Barbados term British Term millwall windmill tower points sails roundhouse cap Survey of current millwalls - October 1999 Note on locations The names given to the location of millwalls in this list are largely of my own making, and may not be accurate. Sugar mills, by their very nature, were associated with plantations, and unless the mill and plantation house have survived together as an identifiable unit, it's not always obvious which plantation the mill went with. Coupling this with the vagueness of exact location that the Barbados maps tend to provide may mean that I have misidentified mills. Locations I am especially unsure or suspicious of I have identified with ?? Morgan Lewis Mill, St Andrew Morgan Lewis mill, commonly given the date c1727, continued to work through until 1945. In 1962 E L Banister donated it to the Barbados National Trust, who commenced a restoration project 2 years later. It was further restored in 1974, but deteriorated again, so much so that it was listed as one of the most endangered heritage sites in the world. However a 2 year restoration by the UK millwrights The Chiltern Partnership, started in 1996, has brought the mill back to its former glory. Coverley, Christ Church This unroofed millwall is in a reasonable state of repair, but does have a tree growing out of it. Graeme Hall, Christ Church In the grounds of a site owned by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development. The tower, now roofed and turretted, bears the date 1929 on the masonry of the turrets above a bell. The tower is of regular coral blocks, and shows signs of conversion from 1 large arch to 2 smaller ones. There is also a further tall, thin arch. Above the main doorway is another date, which reads B.R. 1703 (though the last digit is indistinct). Ealing Park, Christ Church This mill is now bordered by Millwall Avenue, part of the Ealing Park stage 3 development. The millwall itself is constructed of coral blocks, and is in the process of being incorporated into a house conversion. As is the case with much of the new building in Barbados, this conversion is taking its time, and there appears to have been little work for many months. Gibbons, Christ Church This 8 sided structure was considered by Prof Dash to have been an animal rather than a wind-mill. However Rex Wailes did not fully agree with the Professor's findings, and from inspection I can see no reason why this was not considered to be a windmill - excepting the unusual non round base, it has all the features of other definite windmills, including the tall narrow archway. title: Windmills of California
body_text: Windmills of California Windmills of California More material being prepared - Check back again soon! Golden Gate Park There are 2 traditional "Dutch style" windmills in Golden Gate Park, located at the western end to catch the ample sea breezes. The Dutch Windmill The Dutch Windmill was built in 1902, at a cost of $16,000, together with a Dutch Cottage alongside which was occupied by the mill's caretaker. 75 feet high, and 33 feet in diameter at the base, is sails had a span of 102 feet and meant it was capable of pumping 30,000 gallons of fresh water per hour from underground to a reservoir on Strawberry Hill. Despite being a great success for a few years (so much so that a second windmill was built), by 1913 electric pumps were introduced , so the windmills began to become obsolete. Much of the Dutch Mill's machinery was destroyed by a storm in the 1930's, followed by further gutting to aid the 2nd World War effort. In the winter of 1949 one of the sails was blown off, and a few months later the other 3 sails were removed for safety. A Citizens Commission formed in 1964 to start efforts to restore the mills, but despite receiving a Federal grant of $10,000 in 1968, it was not until August 1976 that volunteers from the US Navy Reserve started work on restoring the Dutch Mill . Work continued through to completion in 1981. Since then little additional work has been done, and although, as the many photos of the mill show, from the exterior the mill looks impressive, structurally it's showing signs of decay again . At the base of the mill, the grounds have been laid out as the Queen Wilhelmina Tulip Garden - a fact that contributes to the popularity of the mill as a photo location. It's also given rise to the often repeated, but false story that the mill "was a gift to the city of San Francisco from Holland"! Point to note: Looking at historical pictures of the mill, it's apparent that the "restored" mill's sails rotate in the opposite direction to the original sails! Circa 1940's hand coloured print Dutch Mill in 1999. The Murphy Windmill With the undoubted success of the Dutch Mill , in 1905 a second windmill was built to the south, known as the Murphy Windmill, after Samuel G Murphy who donated $20,000 (one source says $25,000) for its construction. This mill was even larger than the first, 95 feet high, with sails 114 feet across, capable of pumping 40,000 gallons per hour, and survived slightly longer before electric pumps were installed. Sadly this mill has never been restored, and currently stands sailless and neglected, slowly deteriorating. The Murphy Windmill has a concrete base, surmounted by a slate clad wooden upper body, and each year more slates fall from the mill. The remains of the sails are stacked in the undergrowth nearby. Not surprisingly, despite the many web sites with photos of the Dutch Mill , no-one seems to want to put up pictures of the forlorn Murphy windmill. As it was in 1999. title: Chitty Chitty Bang Bang
body_text: Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Chitty Chitty Bang Bang Books Hardback Editions " Chitty Chitty Bang Bang " written by Ian Fleming and illustrated by John Burningham was originally published in hardback in 3 parts Adventure Number 1, Jonathan Cape, London, 1964 Adventure Number 2, Jonathan Cape, London, 1964 Adventure Number 3, Jonathan Cape, London, 1965 The title became " Chitty Chitty Bang Bang - The Magical Car " when the US edition was published as a single book by Random House, New York, Library of Congress catalog number 64-21282 For the benefit of its readers, the US edition contained this additional text at the front of the book: A note for the Observant Reader This story takes place in England and, as in England they use English money - peculiarly enough - the American reader will need to know a little - though not a lot - about English currency. So, a pound is worth approximately $2.80 and a shilling is worth 14 cents. And, if your arithmetic is good enough, you should be able to figure out exactly how much things cost in this story. This same US version was also available as a "Weekly Reader Children's Book Club" edition. In 1976, Aeonian Press Inc, Mattituck, New York, published an edition limited to 250 copies "by special arrangement with Scholastic Magazines Inc". LOC 81-68683, ISBN 0-88411-9831. The UK single book version " Chitty Chitty Bang Bang - The Complete Adventures of the Magical Car " was published by Jonathan Cape, London in 1971, and reprinted in 1977. ISBN 0 224 00535 9 " Ian Fleming's Story of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang - The Magical Car " was 'Adapted for beginning readers by Al Perkins' and Illustrated by B. Tobey. Published by Collins and Harvill, as A Beginner Book, 1969. " The Adentures of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang. A special Motion-Picture Edition " by Albert G Miller 'adapted from the screenplay based on the Ian Fleming story' was published by Collins in 1968, and 'illustrated with photographs from the motion picture'. Random House published the US version of the Motion-Picture edition. The series of books called "Little Golden Book's" featured Chitty Chitty Bang Bang as #C-581 in 1968. A Little Golden Book #00238, with record, 1968. There was also a version in the "Big Little Book" series. Random House also produced a popup version of the book, illustrated from the film, by Gwen Gordon and Dave Chambers. "Meet Chitty Chitty Bang Bang - The Wonderful Magical Car" adapted by Al Perkins from the screenplay. Illustrated by John Hanna, published by Random House, New York, 1968. The book is about 9 1/2" x 12 1/2", and consists of 29 pages. Golden Shape Book number 5945, by Joan Allen, Golden Press, 1968. Paperback Editions " Chitty Chitty Bang Bang " - Signet T3705, Starlight edition published by Scholastic Book Services, USA, 1st printing Nov 1968 (also carries catalog number TK 1389) The cover was changed to a still from the film in time for the 2nd printing Feb 1969, and the catalog number changed to SBS TK1365 The Bullseye B

title: Petsburgh Leaders Guide
body_text: Petsburgh Leaders Guide Petsburgh Community Leader Application Serving Petsburgh and all of its suburbs Thank you for your interest in the Petsburgh Community Leader Program. The CL job can be very rewarding as you help homesteaders build their new homes on the web. This page is designed to answer many of your questions about being a CL. Once you are sure you would like to apply, you can fill out the application. Here are the answers to some questions you may have. What will I do as a CL? Serve as an example to other homesteaders. This includes having good home pages that fit the Petsburgh theme with no content violations, and having a "developed" page. This means it should have at least two sub pages. Monitor specific blocks in your neighborhood (as specified by the Liaison). You'll be looking for great sites and those pages that don't meet the content guidelines, which you will tell Geocities about so they can contact the owners or remove them if necessary; and content that doesn't match the theme of the Petsburgh neighborhood. Act as a liaison between your neighbors and Geocities. Your member name and e-mail address will be posted in a prominent place within the neighborhood so everyone will know who to contact if they have questions or problems. We encourage members to think of you as their primary resource, for everything from HTML problems to content guidelines to neighborhood themes. Some leaders may get 10 and 20 messages a day, sometimes more and most of the time less. Keep your own home page fresh and lively. If we're holding you out as leaders of the community, your own site should be a showcase. It doesn't have to be completely whiz-bang (although your fellow Community Leaders may be able to help you spice it up), but it should be updated at least once a week. It absolutely MUST conform to Geocities content guidelines and to the theme of your neighborhood. If it doesn't, your application will be automatically rejected. Recruit and nominate new Community Leaders by referring those who you think qualify to the Community Leader Application. You will also be asked to vote on applicants. You will be responsible for communicating with your fellow community leaders via email regarding Petsburgh Business. Although not mandatory, your presence is encouraged at the Petsburgh CL meetings held weekly and will help us ensure that Petsburgh is running efficiently. In addition, please notify your Liaison when any change in your email, URL, or committee work occurs. Probably some other things we haven't thought of yet, but we'll let you know when we do. What are the requirements of being a CL? Be an established homesteader in the Petsburgh community. Good HTML knowledge. We will not be able to train you on HTML and you will be answering a lot of HTML questions. Familiar with GeoCities utilities. Complete compliance with the Content Guidelines. We strongly urge you to have the GeoGuide on at least your index.html page. Willingness to help. Good commun

body_text: Community Leader Pride PETSBURGH CL'S ARE PROUD TO BE HERE! TEAM TALK!! From: Lisa - Petsburgh Liaison There is no better team to work with in the years I have been on the net, than Petsburgh personnel. There is no comparison to the camraderie I have found here, and there is no better feeling than getting that simple "thank you" from a homesteader you have helped along the way. This morning I was reminded of someone I helped when I worked with a committee here in Petsburgh....that homesteader just graduated into our family of CLs. She did a full circle and I'm so proud of her. But it's the special situations like this that remind me of just how important we are. Every one of us has a very important message to give to the homesteaders. We are HERE to help THEM. The enjoyment we get from their thanks is just an extra unexpected bonus for us. A pat on the back.... a warm fuzzy feeling. Think of the enthusiasm we have planted in that homesteader on the ladder of learning. THAT is why I enjoy being a Community Leader! Lisa aka birdbaby From SuSue - Petsburgh/Yard Co-Liaison I became a CL because I couldn't find one to help me!! When I first discovered the internet, I found a sign up page on Angelfire. I knew NOTHING about webpage design, not a bit of HTML code (what is that), and did not even know that there was life beyond Angelfire! I was naive to say the least! There was no one to turn to for help, there were no community leaders. They had a very complicated (in my opinion at the time) editor, but I managed to get one page done, with their equivilant of the basic editor. I still have that page. I have updated it once, but it is still ONE page! Its been there for 3 years! Not long after that I found somebody on Angelfire with a link to someone's sight on GeoCities! GeoCities? What is that? Off I went, well the rest is history, I never looked back! First I opened my site in Heartland. http://www.geocities.com/Heartland/Acres/2410 I made my sister open one there too! http://www.geocities.com/Heartland/Acres/2322 We AGONIZED over choosing where to put our sites! We are farm girls you see, and we wanted something that reflected our rural Washington upbringing. We don't have estates, or ranches, or prairies here! But AH HA! We have Acres!! Acres it was! Well neither of us knew diddly about making a home page, but we did know we wanted on! My sister was scared to death of her computer and the internet intimidated her righteously! So I opened her site, and mine. I forced myself to learn how to do this HTML stuff. And finally got a couple of decent pages up for both of us up! I visited other pages and I studied how pages were set up, and I emailed other homesteaders and made a general pest of myself learning how to do this! Our friends got wind of our sudden internet expertise (I use the term losely!) and they wanted a web page. Pretty soon, I had made lots of them and had gotten pretty good at this! I had still not HEARD from a CL! Then while out visiting

title: Community Leader Pride Page Two
body_text: Community Leader Pride Page Two PETSBURGH CL'S ARE PROUD TO BE HERE! TEAM TALK!! From: Ferd - Petsburgh Park Co-Liaison Haah, I've read what some people have said about why they became CLs, and I wanted to present the male engineer point of view. I didn't go through a painful learning process. My background is architecture, engineering, and computer science. I started back when the Internet was still the Arpanet (well, actually, I started in the days of punch cards and teletypes). I ran a mailing list for 15 years, taught programming at the local community college, and *part* of my job has often including being the system administrator for everything from a supermini to a couple of dozen UN*X workstations. I wrote my first web page about 4 years ago. At the time, the only browser was Mosaic and we used HTML 1.0. I like HTML because it is a markup language like TeX (I'm a local TeXpert). One of my hobbies is learning new computer languages, which is one reason why I learned HTML, Perl, and Java. I've even written programs in PostScript; it's not just for printers. Given that background, I decided to become a CL so I could enlighten the masses. That's not meant to be a snobby comment -- I want to help people get over the initial hump in the learning curve. The more people who know how to write good HTML, the more good pages I'll see. I didn't join to meet people; I've had net friends from British Columbia, England, and Australia, and I already get more email than I want. That's why I joined the C&R Committee instead of the Welcome Committee. I don't get much steader email, which I think is mostly because of the block I run. While it contains a few really good sites, it's about 70% NMIYs (yes, I've sent a welcome letter to everyone). I have helped a few people get started, and one person graduated from using GeoBuilder to writing HTML. OTOH, most of the questions I get are from other areas of Petsburgh. They all write back to thank me for helping or to ask more questions. My favorite is the one where the steader thanked me for answering her question nicely instead of saying something nasty (she had misread some instructions). Yeah, maybe I should have a page in Silicon Valley, but I don't want a site about writing HTML. (Maybe someday ....) I started in Heartland because I wanted to create a site about our horses and cats, then I moved to Petsburgh a few days after it opened. Heck, the reason we bought our first horse was so I'd get outside more. I knew almost nothing about horses, and I didn't even know you lead them on the left! HTML, yes; horses, no :-) Since then I've learned to ride and have raised a couple of foals. Lemme sum up this way -- I want to help new steaders learn HTML and good web page design the same way other people have taught me about horses. From: Ferd - Petsburgh Park Co-Liaison Haah, I've read what some people have said about why they became CLs, and I wanted to present the male engineer point of view. I didn't go through a painful learning process. My background is architecture, engineering, and computer science. I started back when the Internet was still the Arpanet (well, actually, I started in the days of punch cards and teletypes). I ran a mailing list for 15 years, taught programming at the local community college, and *part* of my job has often including being the system administrator for everything from a supermini to a couple of dozen UN*X workstations. I wrote my first web page about 4 years ago. At the time, the only browser was Mosaic and we used HTML 1.0. I like HTML because it is a markup language like TeX (I'm a local TeXpert). One of my hobbies is learning new computer languages, which is one reason why I learned HTML, Perl, and Java. I've even written programs in PostScript; it's not just for printers. Given that background, I decided to become a CL so I could enlighten the masses. That's not meant to be a snobby comment -- I want to help people get over the initial hump in the learning curve. The more people who know how to write good HTML, the more good pages I'll see. I didn't join to meet people; I've had net friends from British Columbia, England, and Australia, and I already get more email than I want. That's why I joined the C&R Committee instead of the Welcome Committee. I don't get much steader email, which I think is mostly because of the block I run. While it contains a few really good sites, it's about 70% NMIYs (yes, I've sent a welcome letter to everyone). I have helped a few people get started, and one person graduated from using GeoBuilder to writing HTML. OTOH, most of the questions I get are from other areas of Petsburgh. They all write back to thank me for helping or to ask more questions. My favorite is the one where the steader thanked me for answering her question nicely instead of saying something nasty (she had misread some instructions). Yeah, maybe I should have a page in Silicon Valley, but I don't want a site about writing HTML. (Maybe someday ....) I started in Heartland because I wanted to create a site about our horses and cats, then I moved to Petsburgh a few days after it opened. Heck, the reason we bought our first horse was so I'd get outside more. I knew almost nothing about horses, and I didn't even know you lead them on the left! HTML, yes; horses, no :-) Since then I've learned to ride and have raised a couple of foals. Lemme sum up this way -- I want to help new steaders learn HTML and good web page design the same way other people have taught me about horses. body_text: D's Journal D's Journal 5 most recent entries Date: 2002-09-05 17:20 Subject: Хе-хе =) Security: Public Mood: Садизм - лучший отдых Music: Deep Mix Moscow Очень хочется посмотреть как lugosi будет рвать свои роскошные локоны из-за невозможности послушать эту песенку немедленно, а потом на то, как он рыдая сгрызет свои не менее роскошные когти, когда он таки до нее доберется =) 3 comments | post a comment Date: 2002-09-05 16:30 Subject: привет flamenco от &chicken`а Security: Public Mood: crazy Music: Deep Mix Moscow Вот, яхонтовый просил передать 1 comment | post a comment Date: 2002-09-04 18:19 Subject: Песенка Security: Public Mood: high Music: rybnikov-verish.mp3 Песенка По ( polinezia ) и Вавилова ( vavilov ) Навеяло Временами года По Ты мне веришь post a comment Date: 2002-08-03 23:39 Subject: Православие WOW! Security: Public Mood: отпускное Music: deep.mix.moscow Плавно перетекающий из передачи в передачу Охлобыстин в рясе очень сильно напоминает рекламную кампанию католичества из Догмы и кришнаитствующего Боя Джорджа... При всей моей любви к этому персонажу, поп, рассказывающий в передаче про моду о зимнем фасоне рясы на синтепоне это посильнее, чем Фауст Гёте =) post a comment Date: 2002-07-26 14:22 Subject: AVALON Security: Public Mood: болею я Music: deep mix moscow Вчера с vavilov и lugosi ходили в 35mm на Авалон. Ежели кратко - кино супер, кинотеатр отстой. Начнем с отстоя. Эти жлобы почему-то решили кондиционировать пустой холл, и устроить парилку в зале. Зал и без того не блещет удобством, коленками упираешься в пластиковую спинку кресла впереди (что говорить про Lugosi, с его 2 метрами ног =), а тут еще климат тропического леса. Использовал Vavilova в качестве вентилятора. Теперь о главном. Avalon (Japan 2001) Review Date: 10/6/01 Director: Mamoru Oshii Music: Kenji Kawai Cast: Malgorzata Foremniak Кино-то СУПЕР. Я очень давно ничего такого хорошего с живыми актерами не видел. Вот он, пример глобализации - японско-польский взгляд на матрицу. Кто скажет что такая глобализация - зло, пусть бросит себя головой об камень =) Идея уже стала общим местом - "вся наша жизнь - играааа", но взгляд правильный, злой такой. Сепия, знакомые с детства интерьеры (разрушенные заводы, церквии, классическая точка соцобщепита), офигительное построение кадра, куча приятных мелочей и отсылок - обожаю. Чего стоят русские надписи на компьютерной гусеничной крепости....... Использовал Lugosi в качестве мобильной киноэнциклопедии. За детальным разбором фильма - к нему. PS Скачал OST, который lugosi ночью заслушал до дыр =)) 13 comments | post a comment browse my journal my userinfo my friends my calendar my website

Ими можно было заслушаться , что я собственно и делал... Пойже появился в моей коллекции ' SOLAR FIELDS - REFLECTIVE FREQUENCIES ' , который меня тоже ужасно порадовал. Теперь я изнемогаю от ' AES DANA - SEASON 5 ', которым я с вами и хочу поделиться. Если у кого-то вдруг найдётся ' SOLAR FIELDS - BLUE MOON STATION ' я буду очень рад если вы поделитесь. Звук чем то похож на Psy- Ambient, но с shpongle такое наверно не стоит сравнить, вообщем - СЛУШАТЬ, СЛУШАТЬ, СЛУШАТЬ!!! post a comment User: clubmusic (posted by soda9 ) Date: 2003-03-01 00:34 Subject: несного о миксах #2 Security: Public Mood: все еще колбашусь Music: Danny Howells & Nick Warren - Revelation CD1 еще есть у меня забавная папка на том же фтп (адрес постом раньше), называется house mixes##renaissance отгадайте, что там? правильно восемь миксов renaissance ibiza, по два соответственно deep dish, dave seaman и Danny Howells & Nick Warren. такие дела. качайте и да пребудет с вами 100кб конеект во веки веком. (и неплохо бы чтобы у меня сеть как вчера не рушилась). аминь post a comment User: clubmusic (posted by soda9 ) Date: 2003-03-01 00:26 Subject: немного о миксах #1 Security: Public Mood: колбашусь Music: Renaissance Ibiza - Deep Dish могу похвастаться наличием двух миксов, точнее это вроде как CD1 и CD2. плэйлист за катом. кому интересно - ключевое слово: йошитоши (in house we thrust) ( плейлисты тут ) богацтво это у мен на фтп (ftp://195.133.227.42) в папочке отгадайте какой? правильно, #in house we thrust. найдете в общем:) post a comment User: anonist (posted by kolaborationist ) Date: 2003-02-28 20:32 Subject: давай-давай! [03 Feb 2004| 01:07pm ] I'm going to one of the professional printers here to ask about art prints, to possibly sell some. If you are interested in knowing prices once I find out you can e-mail me (or just leave a comment). I don't know cost, I also don't have the time to make prints myself right now though, which is why I am doing it this way. If it turns out to be ridiculously expensive I'll probably just auction a few or wait until I have the time to do them myself. If you're on my mailing list, don't worry, you'll be informed anyway. title: 0000000: I know, I promised this a long time ago.
body_text: 0000000: I know, I promised this a long time ago. ! ( 0000000 ) wrote, @ 2004 - 02 - 03 13:07:00 I know, I promised this a long time ago. I'm going to one of the professional printers here to ask about art prints, to possibly sell some. If you are interested in knowing prices once I find out you can e-mail me (or just leave a comment). I don't know cost, I also don't have the time to make prints myself right now though, which is why I am doing it this way. If it turns out to be ridiculously expensive I'll probably just auction a few or wait until I have the time to do them myself. If you're on my mailing list, don't worry, you'll be informed anyway. Edit: I can't sell prints of " Higher " because the original has been damaged. (cross post) ( Post a new comment ) (Anonymous) 2004-02-10 07:10 ( link ) hey! could you email me? i dont know your address but i want to by "patchwork" its thomgarsh@wordlnetw.com thanks. looking forward. ( Reply to this ) paivansade 2004-04-04 09:55 ( link ) yeah, i'd also like to buy "patchwork", if you'll ever be selling it :) ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) 0000000 2004-04-04 13:42 ( link ) Hiiighly unlikely that I'll sell the original anytime soon, but I'll try to remember to send you a signed print of it sometime eventually, since you've been so incredibly supportive of me in every way imaginable :') ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) paivansade 2004-04-04 22:59 ( link ) oh! oh! oh! then i would love you forever and a day more instead of just forever!! :) ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) neferet_tiy 2004-04-16 07:20 ( link ) Depending on how much it'd cost, I'd buy a copy of "Observed" if you were to offer prints of it ;) (And I'd beg you to sign it too haha) Yeah this has been up here for a while...but I wanted to come back and see if I missed anything! ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) 0000000 2004-05-18 04:26 ( link ) I don't want to charge people what I'd have to for postage overseas in rolls (how I usually send prints inland), so I'm going to try some other ways like cardboard reinforced envelopes and see if they make it through the mail ok. If that works out, I'll start offering overseas again and will let you know. Yes, I'd sell prints of "Observed," too. The signature on the version you see online was added digitally, it's not on the original watercolour, but I handsign and number prints. Just in case you buy one later and wonder why the sig/num on the print looks different, it's because it's real there ;-) ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) neferet_tiy 2004-05-18 06:52 ( link ) Hehe awesome. title: 0000000: butterfly net
body_text: 0000000: butterfly net ! ( 0000000 ) wrote, @ 2005 - 01 - 08 22:13:00 Current mood: depressed butterfly net ( Post a new comment ) neferet_tiy 2005-01-08 21:26 ( link ) Ahh Percy I love it :) ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) antiprose 2005-01-11 23:05 ( link ) *bows* ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) amoralphreak 2005-01-09 02:43 ( link ) beautiful picture, but what's wrong??? :( ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) antiprose 2005-01-11 23:05 ( link ) oh, what isn't wrong with this world! ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) amoralphreak 2005-01-11 23:35 ( link ) meh. point. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) xpyromania05x 2005-01-09 06:06 ( link ) nice XD....hope u feel ok ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) antiprose 2005-01-11 23:05 ( link ) thanks, i'm dandy. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) silverskytears 2005-01-09 20:03 ( link ) you have always been the definition of 'tortured artist' to me, though I know little of your life. alas that pain is so inspiring. i shall never be a successful poet . . . i am simply not conflicted enough :P i hope this post finds you drinking tea, or some such deliciousness. ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) 0000000 2005-01-09 20:36 ( link ) hibiscus. i hate it. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) silverskytears 2005-01-09 21:18 ( link ) haha alas and possibly also alack hmmm is it one of those with metallic aftertastes? never got a hang of those. all i need is a good strong-brewed mint tea, sweetened and iced. if only it wasn't the middle of winter and such treats practically make me the snow queen! ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) antiprose 2005-01-11 12:42 ( link ) no, i simply never got into these red teas. i mean really, this tastes like dirt. filtered, coloured dirt. who drinks this stuff?!! (i mean besides broke and broken artists who find it in the back of their cupboards when the green tea is gone...) ah yeah, mint is great also. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) silverskytears 2005-01-11 12:48 ( link ) aha! well, no fear, m'love. I am sure I'll be joining you in the broke and broken, though artist was always questionable. by the way, I still have that lovely letter you wrote me on my wall. tangential thought. been reminiscing a lot lately, which I feel is dangerous because at 19 there shouldn't be an awful lot to ruminate on! ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) antiprose 2005-01-11 12:53 ( link ) hm. that's a happy thought. (my scribbles on your wall with a piece of paper between them.) and the icon is tres cute. 19 is old, so old. nearly 2 decades, which is a long word. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) silverskytears 2005-01-11 18:40 ( link ) happy thought for me too! scribbings tend to cheer me greatly. plus thank you . . . I have found that when I get bored I turn to my camera for amusement. 19 is old! And how old are you? Still 8 I hope. :) I seem to recall that as a good age, mostly because I don't remember it! ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) Username: Password: English • Español • Deutsch • Français • Русски

( Read more... ) 6 comments | post a comment Date: 2003-08-14 19:29 Subject: Отдыхаю. Security: Public После всяких страхов и встрясок Москва кажется безопасным и уютным местом.Все дела переделаны, два дня никуда не надо бегать, ничего не надо делать, собаки не пугают, потому что медведи много страшнее, потому что слава богу что это не медведь. Люди тоже не пугают потому что слава богу что не в тайге в тремя пьяными водилами в камазе надо пить водку, иначе получишь в глаз, по улице ходить не страшно потому что слава богу не 5000 километров до дома и 20 км до жилья и не надо шарахатся от шорохов в лесу и неслышно прятатся в кусты от идущего на встречу человека с недобрым взглядом. В кране есть горячая вода и не надо по утрам прыгать в ледяную воду , в плите есть газ и не надо по утрам топить печку что бы сварить чашку чая, теплое одеяло и кровать и не надо греть камень и сушить одежду на костре что бы не дать ночью дуба в палатке. Спать можно спокойно и не надо смотреть через палатку на лес . До дома можно ехать на метро и не надо стоять на трассе и думать застряла ты здесь на ночь или все же доедешь до другого леса , в котором все равно придется ночевать одной. Все это мне нравится, и одно и другое. Мне нравится и застревать на ночь, и дождь и мокрое белье и давать дуба в палатке и нырять в ледяную воду по утрам и греть воду на костре и даже общаться с пьяными водилами посреди тайги и ныкатся от медведя в кустах..хотя это слишком пожалуй сильные впечателения с медведем то. Но все это требует сил, потмоу что цепляет прежде всего тело -ему неудобно и оно начинает ныть, а потом цепляет меня, я боюсь умереть и тоже начинаю ныть. Но сейчас я отдыхаю, и это мне тоже нравится. post a comment Date: 2003-08-14 00:59 Subject: Security: Public Ну, на самолет я ,положим, опоздала... 18 comments | post a comment Date: 2003-08-13 00:15 Subject: Security: Public Посылку отправить не дали. Сказали что нету почтальона у них, и поэтому посылки только в четверг. Удлинили мои раздумья на счет книжек и вещей. Да, мне никогда не стать монахом, я тащу с собой столько вещей что хватит на зимовье роте слонов, плюс все побрякушки и книжки , расстаться с которыми ну нету моих сил. Или 25 килограмм вещей 6 из которых книги, 2 комплектуха, а 5 палатка, спальник, каремат это не так много? Почему то за две недели ничегонеделания не удосужилась встретиться с людьми с которыми хотела встретиться, купить себе варежки, записать диски , постирать вещи, подкрутить розетку и убрать квартиру. Интересно я сделаю это сейчас или буду носится завтра с круглыми глазами пытаясь опоздать на самолет? Даже адреса и телефоны я не записала. Спокойствие постепенно снисходит :) на мою голову. Если с кем не попрощалась или не встретилась - из

title: 00000001: И все же мне плохо , хреново и фигово от
body_text: 00000001: И все же мне плохо , хреново и фигово от Снежный Лев ( 00000001 ) wrote, @ 2003 - 08 - 04 02:22:00 И все же мне плохо , хреново и фигово от того, что люди ведутся на удовлетворение своих желаний и причинют боль другим людям и вообще существам. И ещё мне плохо, хреново и фигово от того что у других людей и существ не выходит разруливать эти ситуации так, что бы они приносили освобождение, а не боль. И от того, что изменить первое и ускорить второе не в моих силах. ( Post a new comment ) palma 2003-08-03 23:42 ( link ) Тань, как называется провинция, из которой этот вкуссссссный Мао Фэн? ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) 00000001 2003-08-04 06:48 ( link ) А я забыла..не то Айхон..не то ещё как то на А. Спрошу в пятницу. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) persistence 2003-08-04 00:56 ( link ) Я тут как раз удовлетворял свои мгновенные желания соглашаясь с твоей точкой зрения об увольнении и раздираемый собственными мыслями по поводу да/нет, я вырулил ситуацию в головную боль, реальную головную боль -вчера промучался весь вечер. Решение пришло с прохладой и ровным осознанием окончания собственной жизни как стремящегося к карьерному и, наверное, профессиональному росту человека. Я пускаю жизнь колыхаться по волнам до того момента, пока плывёт обрубок бревна, за который я ещё держусь. Будущее неважно. Неправильность подхода и решения также неважна. Важна свобода, которую мне хочется сейчас. ( Reply to this ) ( Thread ) 00000001 2003-08-07 03:21 ( link ) а как сегодня? ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) persistence 2003-08-11 03:04 ( link ) А сегодня я наслаждаюсь послеувольнительным периодом, когда все мерзкие процедуры обхода кабинетов за подписями уже пройдены и сижу дома, решив, что пора бы хоть раз да не перевернуть вверх ногами своё единожды принятое решение (знаю, знаю, всё переменчиво и так далее), сижу и пытаюсь войти в свой обычный ритм жизни, иногда оборачиваясь и хмыкая относительно моих прыжков выше головы. Самая интересная проблема, которая передо мной стояла - назвать чего я хочу. Подобно тому, как бабка с дедом маяли золотую рыбку изобретая чего же им на самом деле хочется, я не смог придумать чего хочется мне во вполне конкретной и, казалось бы, моей области жизни. Отсюда я вынес, что, возможно, область перестала быть моей, возможно, мне просто хочется тишины и солнечного света и я пока имею возможность это иметь, пусть оно у меня будет. ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) 00000001 2003-08-12 14:35 ( link ) Ура :) смысл жизни нашелся? ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) persistence 2003-08-13 03:35 ( link ) Нет, скорее я вернулся к корыту чтобы ещё раз подумать :) Удачи тебе, Танья, в твоём полёте. Хочешь - не хочешь, а я буду временами думать как там у тебя всё сложилось - ведь, в некотором роде, ты - вполне заметная песчинка в моём субъективном мире, а я не особо люблю когда "мои" песчинки разбредаются кто куда вне фокуса моего зрения :) ( Reply to this ) ( Parent ) ( Thread ) 00000001 2003-08-13 14:53 ( link ) да уж. спас
